text:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday upgraded its growth forecast for the South Korean economy to 3.9 percent for this year, up 0.6 percentage point from its earlier projection last month, amid the accelerating global semiconductor supercycle.
An IMF delegation, led by mission chief Corinne Delechat, made the forecast after a two-week consultation with key Korean economic and financial institutions, including the Ministry of Finance and Economy. The IMF's World Economic Outlook earlier projected 3.3 percent growth.
The team also said the Korean economy will grow 3.3 percent in 2027, marking growth of more than 3 percent for the second consecutive year.
"The global AI upcycle is providing an exceptional boost to the Korean economy through record-high semiconductor exports, driving strong corporate earnings and fiscal revenue," it said.
It also forecast that inflation will reach 2.7 percent in 2026 and 2.3 percent in 2027 amid strengthening domestic demand.
The IMF team, however, pointed out that the benefits of strong growth have been spreading to the broader economy at a slow pace, with the technology sector largely enjoying the gains.
It called for a carefully coordinated mix of monetary and fiscal policies to help contain aggregate demand pressures while providing targeted support to vulnerable households and firms.
"Sustaining recent gains from the AI upcycle would require addressing longstanding structural headwinds, including rapid population aging, widening regional disparities and uneven productivity growth across firms and workers," the IMF team said.
"Structural reforms should focus on making growth more resilient and inclusive by helping unlock household consumption, enhance investment opportunities and mitigate exposure to external shocks."
The team also welcomed the launch of the Future Fund, a government-led fund financed by additional tax revenue generated from the semiconductor industry boom, saying it would serve as a "fiscal stabilization vehicle."
